claims.claim: newMux only registers GET /{$}; there is no /hello route today.

scenario.then: the response is 200 with body "hello, world"
the response is 405, since only GET is registered for the route

overview.objective: Add a hello endpoint so a caller can get a plain-text greeting back over HTTP.
overview.context: cmd/zing/main.go builds the HTTP server and its routes in newMux; this adds one more GET route beside the existing index handler.
overview.problem: Nothing today answers a plain greeting request, so there is no minimal route that shows the server responding with dynamic text.

goals.goal: GET /hello returns 200 with the text "hello, world" when the process is running

nongoals.nongoal: Accepting a name parameter or personalizing the greeting is out of scope; this is a fixed-text route, not a templated one

design.demo: Starting the server and curling /hello prints "hello, world" with a 200 status, showing the route is live end to end.
design.shape: newMux gains one more route, `GET /hello`, registered beside the existing `GET /{$}` route. Its handler writes a 200 status and a fixed "hello, world" body; it needs no dependencies, so it stays a package-level function like index.

files.file: register the /hello route in newMux and add its handler
add TestHello covering GET and the POST 405 case

tests.test: GET /hello returns 200 and body "hello, world"; POST /hello returns 405

tasks.task: Add the /hello handler and register it in newMux so the demo command above returns 200.

alternatives.alternative: Reuse the index handler for /hello too: rejected, since a plain-text greeting route should not depend on the same path or body as the human-facing page.

risks.risk: A caller expecting a JSON body instead of plain text would need to parse it differently; call this out in the PR description.
